question: Should semantic (meaning-based) search be part of the default setup?
context: Text search + graph walk is built and always on. Semantic search is also built but only activates if Ollama runs locally with an embedding model; it is not running on this machine. Try both in Ctrl+K once Ollama is installed.

options.name: Text search + graph only
options.what_it_is: Finds pages by matching words, then follows map connections to pull in related components. No extra software.
options.how_it_fits_here: Current default in src/store.js search() and context(). Nothing to install.
pros: Graph walk already finds most related context
cons: Misses synonyms ("login" vs "auth") unless the wiki uses both words

options.name: Optional local embeddings via Ollama
options.what_it_is: Ollama runs AI models on your own machine. An embedding model turns each page into a vector so search matches meaning, not just words. Nothing leaves your computer.
options.how_it_fits_here: Already wired: semanticSearch() in src/store.js caches vectors in .agency/.cache, Ctrl+K and agency_search(mode: semantic) use it when Ollama is detected.
pros: Finds related pages with different wording
cons: Needs Ollama installed and a ~270MB model pulled
First index takes a few seconds

recommendation.why: Keeps the default zero-setup while letting you turn on meaning-based search locally with no code change.
recommendation.would_change_mind_if: the AI briefing already finds the right context in practice, then semantic is not worth the install
